questions.title: IdentificationProvider interface shape
questions.context: IDENT-19 locks the path src/shared/adapters/identification-provider.ts (mirroring src/shared/adapters/storage.ts pattern). Open question: what methods does the contract expose? The use-case needs to: (a) call the provider with photos+config, (b) honor a per-call timeout, (c) get a normalized result back, (d) optionally let the router know the static cost-per-call before dispatch.

options.label: Single identify() method, normalized response
options.description: interface IdentificationProvider { identify(input: { photos: PhotoRef[]; signal: AbortSignal; minConfidence: number }): Promise<NormalizedResult>; readonly providerId: string; readonly model: string; readonly costPerCallCents: number; }. Cost is a static property the router reads before dispatch. Smallest surface, matches the StorageAdapter shape.

options.label: identify() + estimateCost(input)
options.description: Adds a separate estimateCost(input) so connectors can return per-call dynamic cost (e.g. OpenAI cost depends on photo count + token estimate). Router consults estimateCost() before each call. More accurate budget tracking; one extra method per connector.

options.label: identify() + healthCheck() + costPerCallCents
options.description: Adds healthCheck() the breaker can use as a half-open probe instead of a real identification call. Static cost stays. More moving parts but cheaper breaker recovery; requires both connectors to expose a real health endpoint.

questions.title: Connector file location
questions.context: Two connectors ship: Plant.id + OpenAI-compat. Storage adapter precedent is src/shared/adapters/supabase-storage.ts. Other providers (auth-adapter, resend-adapter) live closer to their context. Phase 4 D-17 keeps Resend at src/contexts/notifications/infrastructure/resend-adapter.ts.

options.label: Context-local connectors
options.description: src/contexts/identification/infrastructure/providers/plant-id.ts + openai-compat.ts. Matches Phase 4 D-17 (resend-adapter inside notifications context). Bounded-context discipline; the connectors never used outside this context.

options.label: Shared adapter directory
options.description: src/shared/adapters/plant-id.ts + openai-compat-vision.ts alongside supabase-storage.ts. Matches storage precedent; flatter file tree.

options.label: Hybrid — interface in shared, connectors in context
options.description: Interface at src/shared/adapters/identification-provider.ts (locked by IDENT-19) but implementations under src/contexts/identification/infrastructure/providers/. Interface-vs-impl boundary mirrored at the directory level.

questions.title: Provider response normalization
questions.context: Plant.id and OpenAI-compat return different JSON shapes. Backend must filter by min_confidence, sort desc, slice top 3 (IDENT-04). Where does the canonical shape get produced?

options.label: Connector returns canonical shape
options.description: Each connector translates raw provider JSON → { results: Array<{ scientificName, commonName, confidence, raw }> } before returning. Router/use-case operates on uniform data. Translation lives next to the provider quirks. PRD §6 normalized result type lives in src/contexts/identification/domain/.

options.label: Connector returns raw, normalizer in use-case
options.description: Connector returns raw provider JSON wrapped in a tagged union { provider: 'plant-id', raw } | { provider: 'openai-compat', raw }. Use-case calls a normalizer per provider. Raw payload is queryable via Identification.results jsonb (D-06).

options.label: Connector returns canonical + raw alongside
options.description: Connector returns { canonical: NormalizedResult, raw: unknown }. Use-case persists raw into Identification.results (preserves audit trail), uses canonical for filtering/sorting/UI.

questions.title: Provider ordering source
questions.context: IDENT-19 acceptance says 'router uses ProviderBudget.priority ordering' but the existing schema (src/contexts/identification/infrastructure/db/schema.ts) has NO priority column — only provider, purpose, dailyCostCapCents, alertThresholdPct, minConfidence, isActive. Choice has migration consequences.

options.label: Add priority INT column to provider_budgets
options.description: New Drizzle migration adds priority INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 100. Lower number = higher priority. Plant.id seeded priority=10, OpenAI-compat priority=20. Router queries WHERE purpose='identification' AND is_active ORDER BY priority. Operator-tunable per CLAUDE.md hot-reload constraint. Aligns SPEC text with schema.

options.label: Static config in src/contexts/identification/config.ts
options.description: PROVIDER_ORDER = ['plant-id', 'openai-compat'] as const. Router filters DB providers by this order. No migration. Order changes require redeploy — violates CLAUDE.md hot-reload-without-redeploy intent. Faster to ship, weaker on tunability.

options.label: Hardcode in router with DB enable/disable only
options.description: Router has primary=plant-id, fallback=openai-compat hardcoded. ProviderBudget.is_active is the only DB knob. Simplest; gives up runtime ordering.

questions.title: Pre-call cost-ceiling check
questions.context: COST-05 says provider at ceiling → marked unavailable rest of UTC day; router skips. ProviderUsageCounter has a row keyed (provider, purpose, utc_date) with estimated_cost_cents. Question is when/how the router reads it.

options.label: SELECT counter row inside same TX as increment
options.description: Router opens TX, SELECT current counter, compare to ceiling (from cached ProviderBudget), if under → INSERT ON CONFLICT increment, commit, then call provider. If over → skip and try next. Strongest atomicity; transaction held during provider call (long-tx concern).

options.label: Read cached counter, increment after success
options.description: Read counter via in-memory cache (TTL same as budget cache). If under ceiling → call provider. Counter incremented in a separate short TX after the call returns. Simpler; race condition: 2 concurrent calls might both pass the check before either increments. Acceptable if ceiling has small headroom; rejected by COST-09 atomicity AC.

options.label: Atomic INSERT ON CONFLICT in pre-flight, rollback on skip
options.description: TX 1: INSERT ON CONFLICT UPDATE counter+1, SELECT new total, compare to ceiling. If new total > ceiling → mark provider rest-of-day-unavailable + rollback the increment + skip. If under → commit + call provider. Optimistic-then-rollback pattern; satisfies COST-09 atomicity AC.

questions.chat_more: Custom: use a short atomic preflight reservation. In one short transaction, conditionally increment/reserve estimated cost only when current estimated_cost_cents + estimatedCost <= daily_cost_cap_cents, then commit and call the provider outside the transaction. If the reservation cannot be made, mark/skip the provider for the rest of the UTC day and try the next provider. This preserves atomic ceiling enforcement without holding a transaction during provider HTTP latency.

questions.title: Remaining-budget calculation for fallover guard
questions.context: IDENT-18: total wall-clock 50s, per-call 30s, fallover requires ≥10s remaining else short-circuit provider_unavailable. Need a way to track elapsed time across multiple provider attempts inside the use-case.

options.label: Date.now() captured at use-case entry, computed before each attempt
options.description: const start = Date.now(); function remainingMs() { return TOTAL_BUDGET_MS - (Date.now() - start); }. Before each provider call: if (remainingMs() < FALLOVER_FLOOR_MS) → short-circuit. Simple; no library overhead.

options.label: AbortController + timer-based AbortSignal cascade
options.description: Outer 50s AbortController, per-call 30s child AbortController. Provider connector receives signal; on abort, fetch is cancelled. Remaining computed from outer signal's timeout. Cleaner cancellation semantics; more wiring.

options.label: AbortController + computed remaining via Date.now()
options.description: Both: AbortController for cancellation propagation through connector → fetch, plus Date.now()-based remainingMs() for the ≥10s fallover guard decision. The signal handles 'stop the in-flight call'; the Date.now() handles 'should we even start the next call'.

questions.title: Failure recording timing per attempt
questions.context: When the router tries provider A then provider B then both fail, do we write 1 Identification row capturing the final outcome, or 1 row per attempt? IDENT-12/13/15 acceptance criteria all say 'Identification row persisted' on failure (singular). IDENT-08 history says 'lists success + timeout + provider_unavailable attempts' — implying user-facing row per request, not per provider attempt.

options.label: One Identification row per user request
options.description: Single row per POST. failure_reason = most-specific internal reason from the LAST attempt (or first if all timed out). Per-attempt traces go into Sentry breadcrumbs / PostHog properties for ops, not into the user-visible row. History screen shows one row per request. Matches IDENT-08 wording.

options.label: One row per provider attempt + parent_request_id
options.description: Schema migration: add nullable parent_identification_id; failed attempts get rows linked to the parent. History shows only top-level rows. More detailed audit, schema churn, history-query complexity.

options.label: One row per request + provider_attempts JSONB column
options.description: Single row per request with a new provider_attempts jsonb column { attempts: [{provider, failure_reason, latency_ms, attempted_at}] }. Schema migration adds the column. Full audit without the join, but inflates the row size.

questions.title: Breaker state location
questions.context: COST-08 requires per-provider circuit breaker with open / half-open / closed states. Vercel functions are stateless across invocations — anything in-memory dies between requests.

options.label: DB-only — new provider_breaker_states table
options.description: Migration: provider_breaker_states (provider PK, state enum, opened_at, last_failure_at, consecutive_failures, half_open_probe_at). Router reads on each call. Survives Lambda recycling and concurrent invocations. Adds 1 read per identification.

options.label: Hybrid — in-memory cache fronting DB
options.description: Module-level Map<provider, BreakerState> with the same TTL as the budget cache (Q-15). On miss, read DB; on state change, write DB + invalidate cache. Saves a read on warm Lambda. Eventual consistency between Lambda instances during state flips (acceptable: a few wasted calls before caches expire).

options.label: Reuse provider_usage_counters with breaker columns
options.description: Add breaker_state, breaker_opened_at, breaker_failures columns to existing daily counter row. Bounded by utc_date; resets daily naturally. Mixes concerns; daily reset may be wrong if breaker should outlive a UTC day boundary.

questions.title: Breaker thresholds (N consecutive, window, cooldown)
questions.context: Need concrete numbers. Constraints: per-call 30s timeout, daily 50 wall-clock budget per request, $5/day budget per provider, ~50–500 identifications/day across all users at MVP scale.

options.label: Aggressive — N=3, window=2min, cooldown=60s
options.description: 3 consecutive failures within 2 min → open. Cooldown 60s, half-open allows 1 probe. Trips fast, recovers fast. Risk: noisy networks could flap under low traffic.

options.label: Moderate — N=5, window=5min, cooldown=120s
options.description: 5 consecutive failures within 5 min → open. Cooldown 2 min, half-open allows 1 probe. Balanced default for MVP traffic.

options.label: Conservative — N=10, window=10min, cooldown=300s
options.description: 10 consecutive failures within 10 min → open. Cooldown 5 min. Slow to trip, slow to recover. Risk: bleeds budget on bad provider before tripping.

questions.title: Which failures count toward the breaker
questions.context: IDENT-15 (invalid_response) explicitly increments breaker counter. IDENT-13 (timeout) and IDENT-12 (provider_unavailable) are also failure modes. validation_failed (GPS-bearing photo, IDENT-16) is user-error, not provider-error.

options.label: Provider faults only — timeout + 5xx + invalid_response
options.description: Network timeouts, HTTP 5xx, invalid JSON shapes. User-input failures (validation_failed, GPS reject) and 4xx (e.g. provider rejects malformed image as 400) do NOT count. Cleanest signal.

options.label: Provider faults + 4xx
options.description: Adds 4xx because a provider returning 400 on every request is also broken (e.g. API key rotated). Risk: per-image rejects mask real provider issues.

options.label: Any non-success
options.description: Anything that doesn't return >=1 result above min_confidence counts. Simpler logic; trips on legitimate zero-result identifications (IDENT-05). Probably wrong.

questions.title: Atomic counter increment SQL
questions.context: COST-09 acceptance: 'concurrent requests (Promise.all of 10 POSTs) → counter row reflects exactly 10 increments, not less'. Counter row keyed (provider, purpose, utc_date).

options.label: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET request_count = request_count + 1
options.description: Single statement, atomic, no explicit lock. Postgres serializes the conflict-update path automatically. Standard pattern; matches SPEC §COST-09 target wording.

options.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE then UPDATE
options.description: Explicit row lock acquired before increment. Higher latency under contention; equivalent correctness. More code.

options.label: Postgres advisory lock + read-modify-write
options.description: pg_advisory_xact_lock keyed on (provider, utc_date). Most flexible (allows side effects under the lock — e.g. reading other rows atomically), highest overhead. Overkill for a single counter.

questions.title: Cap-check window math
questions.context: Trial: window = [trial_start_date, trial_end_date], daily_cap=5, period_cap=75. Paid: window = [current_period_start, current_period_end], daily_cap=15, period_cap=200. Daily window = current UTC date. Question is where this math lives.

options.label: Repository helper countIdentificationsInWindow(userId, from, to)
options.description: src/contexts/identification/infrastructure/db/identifications.ts exposes count helpers for daily + period windows. Use-case computes window bounds from User+Subscription+IdentificationLimit and calls the helper. Repo is the only Drizzle consumer (PRD §17 D-17).

options.label: Use-case computes counts inline via injected tx
options.description: Use-case opens UoW, reads User+Subscription+IdentificationLimit, runs two count queries inline (daily + period). All logic in one place; mixes domain logic with SQL. Violates D-17 'no Drizzle in route handlers' — also discouraged for use-cases.

options.label: Domain service check-cap(userId) returning {allowed, reason, resetAt}
options.description: src/contexts/identification/domain/check-cap.ts delegates to repository helpers. Use-case calls a single function and gets a verdict. Highest abstraction; one extra layer.

questions.title: Cap + counter + provider call ordering
questions.context: COST-03 acceptance: 'cap check → consent check → counter increment + provider call (atomic)'. The 'atomic' bit is ambiguous — does the provider HTTP call live inside the increment TX or not? A long-running TX (30s provider call) holds Postgres locks.

options.label: Cap → Consent → TX{counter inc} commit → Provider call → TX{Identification row write}
options.description: Three short transactions. Counter incremented atomically, committed, then provider called outside any TX, then row written. If provider crashes mid-flight, counter is incremented but no row exists — reconciler-style backfill needed for accuracy. Best perf, weakest consistency.

options.label: Cap → Consent → TX{counter inc + Identification 'in_progress' row} → Provider call → TX{update row to success/failed}
options.description: Pre-write a row with status='in_progress' alongside counter inc. If provider crashes, row exists for the reconciler to mark failed. Schema needs 'in_progress' added to status enum (currently only success/failed). One extra DB write per request.

options.label: Cap → Consent → single TX{counter inc + provider call + row write}
options.description: All inside one TX as the SPEC text suggests. Provider call holds the TX open up to 30s. Postgres lock pressure under load + risk of TX timeout misalignment with HTTP timeout. Strongest consistency, worst scaling.

questions.title: Cache location
questions.context: COST-10 requires DB updates to IdentificationLimit + ProviderBudget take effect on next request past TTL. Vercel functions are stateless across cold starts but warm Lambdas reuse module memory.

options.label: Module-level Map per Lambda instance
options.description: const cache = new Map<string, {value, expiresAt}>() at module scope. Survives within a warm Lambda. Each Lambda instance has its own copy → up to {N_lambdas * TTL} delay before all see new values. Simple; no infra dependency.

options.label: Vercel KV or Upstash Redis
options.description: Shared cache across all Lambdas. Stronger consistency on operator updates. Adds infra dependency + cost (Vercel KV pricing or Upstash free tier). Out of CLAUDE.md tech stack — not currently approved.

options.label: No cache — DB read every request
options.description: Both tables are tiny (a handful of rows). Postgres can serve them <1ms. Eliminates the staleness issue entirely. Costs ~2 extra reads per identification request. Simplest correctness.

questions.title: Cache TTL value
questions.context: Only relevant if Q-14 picks (a) module-level cache. Operator runtime tuning expectations: a budget bump should take effect 'soon' but not necessarily instantly. Phase 5 D-17 used 24h for catalog query persistence (different concern).

options.label: 60 seconds
options.description: Operator change visible within 60s on each Lambda. Bounded staleness, acceptable for non-emergency tuning. Minimal cache hit rate cost.

options.label: 300 seconds (5 min)
options.description: Higher cache hit rate; 5-minute window before a cap bump propagates. Acceptable for budget tuning, possibly too slow for emergency provider disable.

options.label: Configurable via env (default 60s)
options.description: CACHE_BUDGET_TTL_SECONDS env var, default 60. Operator can dial to 0 (effectively no cache) for emergency mode without redeploy of business code.

options.label: N/A — Q-14 picked no-cache
options.description: Skip this question if Q-14 = (c).

questions.title: Modal trigger placement
questions.context: IDENT-02: first identification ever without identification_third_party consent triggers modal disclosing both providers + Art. 33; no provider call until granted. Question: when in the user flow does the modal appear?

options.label: Gate at Identify CTA tap (before camera/picker opens)
options.description: Tapping the camera button on /identify checks consent first. If missing → modal. User decides before taking a photo. Cleanest mental model; the user is committing to identification, not just exploring the screen.

options.label: Gate at submit (after photos chosen)
options.description: User can capture photos freely; modal appears when they tap 'Identificar'. Less disruptive to exploration; risk of feeling 'bait-and-switch' if user already invested in capture.

options.label: Gate at Identify screen entry
options.description: Modal blocks the screen on first visit until consent granted (or user backs out). Most explicit; arguably too aggressive (blocks viewing the capture guide).

questions.title: Provider naming in disclosure
questions.context: Art. 33 LGPD requires disclosing the recipients of international transfer. SPEC IDENT-02 acceptance: 'modal listing both provider names + Art. 33 international transfer'.

options.label: Real names — 'Plant.id (Kindwise) e provedor compatível com OpenAI'
options.description: Maximum transparency. Names are public anyway. Couples copy to specific vendors — vendor swap requires copy update + re-consent.

options.label: Generic — 'provedores de IA terceirizados nos EUA e Europa'
options.description: Names not pinned, jurisdiction stated. Future vendor swap doesn't trigger re-consent prompt. Weaker on transparency; ANPD interpretation risk.

options.label: Real names + 'or equivalent successors' clause
options.description: Names today + legal-style escape clause. Transparent on current state, future-proofed for swap. Read-aloud copy gets clunky.

questions.title: Consent grant submission endpoint
questions.context: src/contexts/iam/application/record-consent.ts already exists (Phase 4) with input.purpose='identification_third_party' recognized. src/contexts/iam/api/consent-route.ts is the existing diagnostics consent route. Question: does the modal POST to a new identification-specific endpoint or reuse?

options.label: Reuse existing /api/v1/iam/consent endpoint
options.description: Modal calls the existing consent endpoint with purpose='identification_third_party'. ConsentLog row written with the active policy_version. Zero new endpoints. Consent logic stays in one place.

options.label: New dedicated /api/v1/identifications/consent endpoint
options.description: Phase 6 ships its own consent endpoint that wraps recordConsent({purpose:'identification_third_party'}). Cleaner separation per bounded context; one extra route handler that is essentially a pass-through.

options.label: Inline grant — POST /v1/identifications carries grant_consent: true field
options.description: First identification request with grant_consent=true creates the ConsentLog row + proceeds. No separate request. Coupled flow; consent grant is a side effect of an identification call.

questions.title: Photo capture flow (1..N photos)
questions.context: IDENT-17: accepts 1..N photos with capture guide visible. Phase 5 D-15 photo-journal uses bottom-sheet single-photo flow. The Identify capture is multi-photo by design.

options.label: Single batch picker + thumbnails strip
options.description: User taps camera button → native multi-select picker (or sequence in single capture session). Selected photos render as a horizontal thumbnails strip with [+] add-more affordance and [×] remove. One Identificar button submits all. Familiar mental model.

options.label: Capture-then-confirm sequential loop
options.description: Tap → capture/select 1 photo → preview → 'Adicionar mais?' or 'Identificar'. Loop until user submits. More guided, slower. Better for users uncertain about multi-photo benefit.

options.label: Always allow N from start, default to 1
options.description: Picker accepts up to N (cap configurable, e.g. 5) at any time. Pre-checked default = 1 photo if user hesitates. Hybrid; balances casual vs careful users.

questions.title: Loading state messaging
questions.context: Identification can take up to 30s (per-call cap). UI-06 includes 'loading' state. Phase 3 D-25 ships <Skeleton> with 300ms gate + 120ms fade + reduced-motion fallback. Capture-to-result is the longest single wait in the app.

options.label: Single skeleton with brand copy 'Identificando…'
options.description: Phase 3 Skeleton component with 'Identificando sua planta…' Source Serif 4 headline above. No progress bar, no stage messages. Honest about uncertainty; PRD §17 anti-fake-precision posture.

options.label: Multi-stage messages with skeleton
options.description: Stage 1 'Carregando fotos…' (~2s), stage 2 'Analisando com IA…' (until response). Two-stage messaging from a setTimeout. More feedback; risk of 'stage 2' hanging visibly when provider is slow.

options.label: Skeleton + cancel button after 10s
options.description: Single skeleton; after 10s a 'Cancelar' button fades in (still respecting reduced-motion). User can abort. UI cancels client-side; server-side request still completes per IDENT-14. More user agency; client/server divergence.

questions.title: Manual correction surface
questions.context: IDENT-07: manual correction stored in manual_correction; resolved by name match (case-insensitive) → species_id, else null + Species flag. Question: where does the user enter it?

options.label: Inline 'Não é nenhuma destas?' link under top-3 results
options.description: Link under the results list opens a small input + submit. User types the species name (e.g. 'Monstera deliciosa'). Available alongside selection of any of the top-3. Good for partial-confidence cases.

options.label: Only on zero-results screen (no top-3 returned)
options.description: Manual correction available only when provider returned no results above threshold. Cleaner mental model; users who got top-3 still proceed via selection. Loses correction when results exist but are wrong.

options.label: Both — under results AND on zero-results
options.description: Available on both screens. Most flexibility; biggest UI surface to build.

questions.title: Read-only paywall surface for identify
questions.context: IDENT-21: read-only mode shows 'Reative sua assinatura para identificar novas plantas.' Phase 3 D-25 ships <ModalSheet> (Radix Dialog wrapper). Phase 5 D-21 stubs useSubscription() returning readOnly: false (Phase 10 wires real Stripe).

options.label: ModalSheet with literal copy + reactivate CTA
options.description: Tap Identify CTA in read-only → ModalSheet opens with the locked copy + 'Reativar assinatura' Canopy primary CTA linking to /settings/subscription. Phase 5 D-21 hides mutating affordances; Phase 6 surfaces an explicit paywall on Identify only.

options.label: Inline read-only banner replaces capture controls
options.description: Identify screen renders the persistent read-only banner (Phase 5 D-21) full-width across the capture area. CTA inline. Less interruptive; possibly less attention-grabbing for the reactivate signal.

options.label: Full-page redirect to subscription paywall
options.description: Read-only user navigating to /identify → server redirect to /settings/subscription. Most heavy-handed; loses the 'this is what you would identify' framing.

questions.title: ConfidenceLadder component location & API
questions.context: UI-15: 3 states (high ≥70%, medium 40–69%, low threshold–39%) with redundant signals (bar + segments + percentage + SR label). Reusable component (Phase 7 care guide may reuse for augmented-content trust signals).

options.label: src/shared/ui/confidence-ladder.tsx, prop = confidence number
options.description: <ConfidenceLadder confidence={0.74} /> derives state internally from thresholds (also exported as constants). Caller passes raw 0..1 number. Component is self-contained; thresholds change in one place.

options.label: src/shared/ui/confidence-ladder.tsx, prop = level enum
options.description: <ConfidenceLadder level='high' percentage={74} />. Caller computes level (or repository returns it). Component renders. Caller controls; risk of inconsistent thresholding across surfaces.

options.label: Context-local at src/contexts/identification/ui/confidence-ladder.tsx
options.description: Tied to identification context. Phase 7 builds its own equivalent if needed. Bounded-context discipline; potential duplication.

questions.title: Results layout on the Identify screen
questions.context: UI-06 lists 'results (top 3 cards)' as a state. Top-3 card composition: photo + scientific name (italic, lang='la') + common name + ConfidenceLadder + 'Adicionar à minha estante' CTA. Mobile-first viewport.

options.label: Vertical card stack (one per result)
options.description: Three cards stacked vertically, full-width minus padding. Each card has photo, names, ladder, CTA. Tap anywhere on the card → selection sheet. Standard mobile pattern.

options.label: Top-result hero + 2 alternative cards
options.description: Result #1 rendered large with prominent CTA. Results #2 and #3 below as compact rows ('Outras possibilidades'). Asymmetric hierarchy; signals provider's confidence ranking. Risk: nudges users away from #2/#3 when the model is unsure.

options.label: Equal-prominence vertical cards (no hero)
options.description: Same as (a) but with explicit 'Resultados ordenados pelo nível de confiança' caption. Equal visual weight to honor the 'no fake confidence' constraint while keeping ranking visible via the ladder.

questions.title: Selection → Plant create flow
questions.context: IDENT-06: 'User selects a result and confirms → Plant created linked to Species, name pre-filled, Identification.plant_id FK set'. The create-plant identification branch already exists at src/contexts/catalog/application/create-plant.ts:101-121.

options.label: One-tap 'Adicionar' → straight to plant profile
options.description: Tap CTA on a result card → server creates Plant with default name (species common name pt-BR) + species_id + identification photos as cover/journal entries → user lands on /catalog/{plantId}. Fastest; matches <2-min core value promise.

options.label: Intermediate confirmation sheet
options.description: Tap CTA → ModalSheet with name (editable), location (Combobox from Phase 5 D-08), notes (optional) → 'Confirmar'. Then navigate to plant profile. Captures location at creation time; adds a step.

options.label: Pre-filled add-plant page
options.description: Tap CTA → navigate to /catalog/add with name + species_id + photos pre-filled. User reviews/edits + submits. Reuses Phase 5 manual-add page; full flexibility; slowest. Risk: feels redundant after just selecting a species.

questions.title: Identification photo upload route
questions.context: Phase 2 ships POST /api/v1/photos/upload (single photo, returns { photoUrl, thumbnailUrl }). Identification needs 1..N photos. Reuse vs context-specific multipart.

options.label: Single multipart POST /v1/identifications with all photos
options.description: Client sends multipart with N photo parts + metadata in one request. Server uploads each (per-photo MIME/size/GPS guard) inside the use-case before calling provider. Atomic; fewer round-trips; longer single request.

options.label: Pre-upload via existing /v1/photos/upload, POST identifications with photo_urls[]
options.description: Client uploads each photo via existing endpoint, gets URLs back, then POSTs JSON {photo_urls: [...]} to /v1/identifications. Reuses Phase 2 plumbing; multiple round-trips; client-side orchestration; risk of orphaned photo bytes if user abandons.

options.label: Context-specific /v1/identifications/photos pre-upload + JSON identifications POST
options.description: New endpoint /v1/identifications/photos uploads to a temp prefix; identifications POST consumes refs. Cleanup cron deletes orphans after 24h. Adds infra; cleanest separation.

questions.title: Identification.photo_urls persistence shape
questions.context: Schema: photo_urls TEXT[]. Phase 5 D-20 mints 24h-TTL signed URLs at read time, stores raw bucket/key in DB. Phase 5 catalog photos use bucket=plant-photos.

options.label: Store {bucket}/{key} refs; sign at history-screen read time
options.description: photo_urls = ['plant-photos/{userId}/identifications/{idId}/{photoId}.jpg']. History screen mints signed URLs on render. Matches Phase 5 D-20 pattern. Renderer needs to know bucket conventions.

options.label: Store full bucket+key+ext in JSON, sign on read
options.description: photo_urls = ['{"bucket":"...","key":"...","ext":"jpg"}']. Self-describing. Schema is text[], so requires JSON.parse at read.

options.label: Dedicated identification_photos bucket
options.description: New bucket 'identification-photos' separate from plant-photos. Storage admin can apply different retention/cost rules. Cross-flow when selection→Plant creation needs to reference (move bytes, share keys, or duplicate).

questions.title: Server-side EXIF/GPS guard reuse
questions.context: IDENT-16: server rejects GPS-bearing photos as validation_failed. Phase 2 D-30 + INFRA-19 ship rejectGpsMetadata in src/shared/images/server-validate.ts. Already used by /api/v1/photos/upload and src/contexts/catalog/application/create-plant.ts.

options.label: Call rejectGpsMetadata per photo inside the use-case
options.description: Use-case loops over uploaded photos, calls rejectGpsMetadata(buffer) for each, returns validation_failed on first hit. Identical to create-plant.ts pattern. Centralized in identification use-case.

options.label: Centralize in route handler before reaching the use-case
options.description: Route handler runs the guard on each multipart part as it parses, then passes safe buffers to the use-case. Use-case stays focused on identification logic. Splits validation across layers (already the create-plant.ts approach for MIME/size at use-case level).

options.label: New shared helper validateIdentificationPhotos(photos[])
options.description: Wrap rejectGpsMetadata + size + MIME in a single helper specific to identification's 1..N batch. Use-case calls once. Reusable across pre-upload routes if Q-26 picks (b) or (c).

questions.title: History screen pagination
questions.context: UI-12 + IDENT-08: per-user list of all Identifications. Phase 2 D-36 ships cursor pagination contract. Phase 5 D-12 uses opaque base64 cursor for catalog. Volume per user: trial 75/period, paid 200/period — small.

options.label: Cursor pagination (matches Phase 2 D-36 + Phase 5 D-12)
options.description: Opaque base64 cursor encoding {created_at, id}. Page size 50 default, 200 max. Matches established pattern. Probably overkill for typical user volume but stays consistent.

options.label: Last-30-days window + 'Ver mais' loads previous 30d
options.description: Default view: last 30 days. Older requests behind a CTA. Volume-friendly UI; no cursor complexity for typical users.

options.label: Single page — no pagination (volume guard)
options.description: MVP volume is bounded (75–200 per period). One page suffices. Server caps response at 200. Pagination added if/when needed. Simplest.

questions.title: 80% cost-alert idempotency mechanism
questions.context: COST-04: 'second identification at 81% does not duplicate the alert' — exactly one email per provider per UTC day. Operator email goes through existing notifications/send-email Inngest function (Phase 4).

options.label: Add alert_sent_at column to provider_usage_counters
options.description: Migration: alert_sent_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL on the existing daily counter row. Cap-check use-case sets it inside the same TX as the increment that crosses 80%. Email dispatched only if column was NULL at TX entry. One DB column, no new table.

options.label: Separate provider_cost_alerts table
options.description: (provider, purpose, utc_date) PK row inserted ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Email dispatched only on successful insert. Audit-friendly; new table to maintain.

options.label: Inngest event idempotency key
options.description: Emit notifications/email.requested with idempotency key 'cost-80pct-{provider}-{utc_date}'. Inngest dedups same-day repeats. Free-tier behavior depends on Inngest's idempotency window — verify before relying.

questions.title: Provider stub strategy under IDENTIFICATION_PROVIDER_MODE
questions.context: Phase 1 ships IDENTIFICATION_PROVIDER_MODE env gating stub vs real (CLAUDE.md INFRA-26 + Phase 1 SC-5). Phase 6 lands the real connectors and the stub. Stub must support all SPEC tests (timeout, invalid_response, malformed, sub-threshold, etc.).

options.label: Two stub connectors that read scenario from request header/env
options.description: PlantIdStubConnector + OpenAiCompatStubConnector implementing IdentificationProvider. Read X-Test-Scenario header (only honored when MODE=stub) — values like 'timeout', 'sub-threshold', 'invalid-response', 'success-monstera'. Predictable; couples test-only branching into the codebase.

options.label: MSW HTTP intercepts in tests; real connectors against intercepts
options.description: Real connectors run unchanged. Tests start MSW worker with handlers per scenario. Stubs the network layer, not the connector layer. Tests exercise real connector code; MSW dependency only in test bundle. Higher fidelity.

options.label: Per-test injected mock connectors via __setProviderForTests test seam
options.description: Mirror Phase 5 D-27 __setStorageAdapterForTests pattern. Integration tests inject deterministic mock connectors. Connector internals not exercised by integration tests (separate unit tests cover them).

questions.title: PostHog event firing layer
questions.context: Constraint: 'PostHog event taxonomy includes identification_started, identification_succeeded, identification_cap_hit (per OBS-03 — wired in this phase for those three events)'. Phase 1 D-21 + Phase 5 D-28/29 fire server-side via posthog-node from route handlers / use-cases.

options.label: All three server-side via posthog-node
options.description: identification_started fired in route handler at request entry (after JWT). identification_succeeded fired post-TX-commit in use-case. identification_cap_hit fired in cap-check use-case before short-circuit. Matches Phase 5 D-28/29 server-only pattern. Privacy-clean (no PII).

options.label: Started client-side, succeeded + cap_hit server-side
options.description: identification_started client-side from Identify screen submit handler (more accurate funnel start); the rest server-side. Two transports; Phase 1 D-21 client posture (autocapture:false, identified_only) preserved. More wiring.

options.label: All client-side from results/error screens
options.description: All three from client. Simplest funnel attribution; server-side TX commit doesn't gate the event so order can be wrong. Doesn't fire if user closes the tab mid-request (per IDENT-14 the row persists but the event wouldn't). Wrong fit.
